newLayers.name: Serialization
newLayers.description: How Spark turns objects into bytes: the Serializer and SerializerInstance abstraction, the Java and Kryo serializers, the SerializerManager that chooses a serializer per block, a serialization debugger for finding the field that cannot be serialized, and the Avro helper.

appendDesc.Executor, Environment and Deploy: Also covers executor metrics (ExecutorMetrics, the poller and sources), the executor class loader, exit codes and the task level input and output metrics.
appendDesc.Shuffle and Block Storage: Also covers push based shuffle on the map side (ShuffleBlockPusher), checksums, shuffle metrics reporters and the sort data format.

tour.title: Serializers
tour.description: Data crossing a process or disk boundary must be serialized. Serializer creates SerializerInstances; JavaSerializer is the default Java implementation and KryoSerializer is a faster alternative that registers classes. SerializerManager picks the serializer and compression for each block depending on its type and where it is stored, and SerializationDebugger explains which field made a Java serialization fail.

tour.title: Executor metrics
tour.description: Executors report resource usage in two ways. Per task, TaskMetrics holds input, output and shuffle numbers (InputMetrics, OutputMetrics and the shuffle reporters). Per executor, ExecutorMetricsPoller samples JVM and memory metrics and ExecutorMetrics carries them to the driver, while ExecutorSource and ExecutorMetricsSource expose them to the metrics system.
